text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bunds religiously followed U.S. Treasuries lower in late European trade, lacking enthusiasm to break out of their recent range before a national holiday in Germany on Thursday. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.75, down 0.11 from Tuesday's settlement price.
BRITAIN - UK gilts slipped off their highs on Wednesday and settled 4/32 down on the day. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-08/32, down 05/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - June bond future settled little changed after trading in narrow range ahead of public holiday on Thursday. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 124.60 up 0.28 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and Btp futures closed steadily firmer but off session highs, continuing the rally seen in futures on hopes of an early Bank of Italy interest rate cut. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.13 up 0.30 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries weakened in mid-morning activity. 2.0 pct Q1 productivity rise was offset by 2.7 pct unit labor cost gain. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-22/32, down 13/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.93 percent.

JAPAN - Key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed slightly firmer on Wednesday after recouping sharp morning losses. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 124.60, up 0.28 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Five-year dollar bonds proved to be the flavour of the day on Wednesday, with sizeable fixed transactions and also some FRNs seen. Landesgirokasse Oeffentliche Bank and Landesparkasse (LGK) launched its dollar benchmark bond, a $500 million five-year deal, which paid 13 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes. The triple-A rated German bank had held an extensive roadshow in Asia and Europe before launching the deal, and a syndicate manager at joint lead CSFB said the transaction had been well-received as a result.
